Chapter 5: Building an Inclusive and Honest Feminism
Let’s dive into what it really means to build a feminism that’s both honest and inclusive.
At its heart, feminism isn’t about drawing lines or creating new divisions. It’s about opening doors—and making space for everyone to truly be themselves.
But for feminism to be that powerful force, it has to be willing to listen, to welcome in all voices, and to speak the truth, even when it’s hard.
Think about how many different ways there are to be a woman—and how many unique experiences of inequality exist. Race, class, sexuality, and so many other factors shape how each person moves through the world.
If feminism ignores those differences, it risks leaving people behind. Real progress? It’s about recognizing that not all women face the same challenges—and that some carry more privilege than others.
Picture a group of friends, each with her own story. One faces discrimination because of her skin color. Another, because of her sexuality. And another, because she’s struggling to make ends meet.
Their struggles aren’t the same—but what brings them together is a shared desire for respect and dignity. When they listen to one another and offer support, their voices naturally become stronger.
Honesty plays a huge role here. It’s easy to talk about equality in theory, right? But it’s much harder to face up to the ways that privilege and bias creep into our everyday lives. Sometimes, it means admitting you made a mistake, or recognizing a blind spot. It means staying open to learning, to changing, and to doing better.
And let’s be clear—feminism isn’t just for women. Men are shaped by gender roles too. They have a stake in building a more equal world.
When men feel free to show their feelings, to care for their families, or to define success on their own terms, everyone benefits. Those old rules? They end up hurting everyone, just in different ways.
The path forward isn’t always simple. There will be disagreements, setbacks, and moments where things just feel tough. But the goal stays the same: a world where every single person is valued, where no one is held back by gender, and where fairness is just the way things are.
Building this kind of feminism—it takes courage. It takes humility. And it definitely takes hope. It means asking tough questions, being willing to hear uncomfortable answers, and never settling for less than true equality.
It’s a journey, not a destination. And the best part? This journey belongs to everyone.
